phase.title: Core contracts and bounded agent loop
phase.goal: Implement transport-independent execution contracts, a pure bounded Agent Loop, and a minimal in-memory Agent Harness.

why_this_phase_exists: Prove the real execution algorithm and lifecycle boundary deterministically before adding MCP, persistence, RPC, or a real provider.
implementation_guidelines: Follow docs/requirements/project-brief.md: Keep implementation clean and Retry and cancellation ownership by phase.
Keep the loop readable top to bottom; reuse ToolResult factories, serialization, cancellation signals, and the existing event collector.
Do not add a retry framework, SDK branches, or speculative async wrappers to the core.
in_scope: Define typed core models for Session, Run, Message, ModelResponse, ToolCall, ToolResult, Event, RuntimeError, ExecutionLimits, and Usage.
Define an LLM provider interface that hides provider-specific SDK types.
Define a small provider-neutral ToolDefinition contract so later phases can pass approved tool schemas to the model.
Define a tool executor interface that the loop can call without knowing about MCP transport details.
Implement a multi-step agent loop that feeds tool results back to the model before requesting the next step.
Implement a minimal in-memory Agent Harness that owns Run lifecycle, execution state, limits, cancellation signals, and event coordination around the loop.
Define the small Run lifecycle: queued, running, cancel_requested, completed, failed, cancelled, limit_exceeded, and interrupted.
Enforce bounded execution using configurable model-step, tool-call, and overall deadline concepts without choosing production defaults.
Emit a small set of ordered, structured events for meaningful execution transitions.
Collect events for each Run in an in-memory list exposed for direct test inspection, using InMemoryEventCollector or an equivalent simple mechanism.
Provide a small optional developer-only renderer for the current event trace, usable in terminal debug runs and failed-test diagnostics without changing execution behavior.
Normalize provider and tool failures into RuntimeError instead of exposing raw exceptions.
Build simple deterministic FakeLLMProvider and FakeToolExecutor test doubles behind the real core interfaces.
out_of_scope: Writing event history to JSON, JSONL, SQLite, Postgres, or any other durable storage
Network logging and a full CLI or TUI
Durable cancellation and cancellation of in-flight external I/O
Automatic retries, retry delays, backoff, jitter, and adapter attempt events
A universal provider framework or a large event taxonomy
boundaries_introduced: AgentLoop owns only the model-tool-result cycle and its bounded termination mechanics.
AgentHarness owns Run lifecycle, inspectable in-memory state, execution limits, cancellation signals, and event sequencing.
An in-memory collector retains the ordered events coordinated by the Harness; tests and an optional terminal renderer consume that list.
Terminal rendering belongs outside the Agent Loop and only reads collected events; the loop must not print, format terminal output, or depend on the renderer.
LLMProvider isolates provider request, response, and error formats from the loop.
ToolExecutor isolates tool transport and execution details from the loop.
Core contracts are typed and JSON-serializable but contain no raw SDK objects.
contracts_introduced: Session and Run remain distinct: a Session is a context container and a Run is one execution attempt.
Message and Event remain distinct: a Message participates in model context and an Event records a runtime fact.
ToolCall contains a tool_call_id, tool name, structured arguments, and run_id where useful.
ToolDefinition contains a tool name, description, and JSON-serializable parameter schema.
ToolResult contains tool_call_id, tool_name, status, model_content, RuntimeError when present, and minimal runtime metadata.
RuntimeError contains code, message, retryable, and JSON-serializable details.
Event contains event_id, session_id, run_id, monotonically increasing per-Run sequence, type, timestamp, and payload.
Every Event, including its payload and timestamp, can be converted to JSON-compatible data and serialized without raw SDK objects or lossy string fallbacks.
The collector holds events: list[Event] for one execution and makes the full sequence directly inspectable during the test or process lifetime.

termination: Finish when the model returns a final answer without tool calls.
Fail on an unrecoverable provider or internal error.
Stop before scheduling more work when cancellation is observed.
Stop with limit_exceeded when a configured step, tool-call, or overall deadline is exhausted.
execution_policy.tool_results: Keep model-visible content separate from runtime error and metadata; make the normalized result available to the next model step only when policy permits continuation.
execution_policy.errors: Convert provider and tool failures to RuntimeError; raw SDK exceptions are never core outputs.
execution_policy.retry: No automatic retry. Provider exceptions fail the run; tool failures become model input. RuntimeError.retryable is metadata only. A model-requested repeat is a new logical call charged to normal loop budgets.
execution_policy.checkpoint_limitations: The original Phase 1 implementation checked only scheduling checkpoints and could not interrupt blocked calls or reject all late output. Phase 2 subsequently upgrades these ports and the loop to async, adds bounded I/O and post-operation cancel/deadline checks. Arbitrary blocking synchronous code is still not forcibly interruptible. Phase 3 adds durable cancellation/completion race handling.
execution_policy.cancellation: The Harness supplies a cancellation signal and the loop checks it before scheduling each new model or tool step.
execution_policy.event_ordering: The in-memory Harness coordinates monotonically increasing per-Run event sequence numbers; the loop does not know about a database or network stream.

event_inspection_policy.storage: Keep the ordered event history in process memory only. Events are lost when the process exits; no database, JSON file, JSONL file, or network sink is used in Phase 1.
event_inspection_policy.ownership: The Harness remains responsible for event coordination and sequence numbers. InMemoryEventCollector or an equivalent list-backed mechanism only collects the emitted events for a Run.
event_inspection_policy.test_inspection: Tests inspect the event list directly for event types, Run identifiers, ordering, payloads, expected terminal outcomes, failure paths, and cancellation lifecycle events.
event_inspection_policy.serialization: Test conversion of each Event to JSON-compatible data and JSON serialization entirely in memory. Reuse this Event contract for persistence in Phase 3 and RPC/event streaming in Phase 4.
event_inspection_policy.terminal_debugging: An optional small presentation helper renders the Run identifier, ordered sequence numbers, event types, and useful model/tool result or error details from the collected list. It may return text for the caller to print and must not mutate events or influence loop behavior.
event_inspection_policy.failed_tests: Make the same trace easy to include in a failed assertion or pytest diagnostic output. Structured event assertions remain the correctness checks; terminal formatting is only a debugging aid.
event_inspection_policy.visibility: In-memory does not mean invisible: pytest, the developer renderer, and local debugging tools can inspect the current execution history while the process is alive.

deliverables: Minimal in-memory Agent Harness and inspectable execution state
Simple per-Run in-memory event collector with a directly inspectable ordered Event list
Optional lightweight terminal trace renderer usable in local debug runs and failed-test diagnostics
Simple deterministic fake provider and tool executor
Unit tests for the loop and state transitions

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A deterministic test performs at least one tool call, feeds its result into a later model request, and then completes with a final answer.
Every model step, tool request, tool result, status transition, normalized error, and final output is inspectable as typed state or a structured event.
Configured limits prevent an endlessly tool-calling fake model from running forever.
The core has no dependency on HTTP, RPC, an MCP SDK, or a provider-specific SDK.
The pure Agent Loop can be tested using FakeLLMProvider and FakeToolExecutor without importing a real provider SDK, RPC framework, MCP SDK, or database.
Provider failures, tool failures, and malformed model tool calls become structured RuntimeError outcomes rather than raw exceptions.
Events are collected in memory in execution order, and tests can directly inspect the full event list with strictly increasing sequence numbers within a Run.
Tests verify the expected terminal event, failure events, and cancellation lifecycle events for their corresponding execution paths.
Every collected Event can be converted to JSON-compatible data and serialized in memory, including payloads on success, failure, and cancellation paths.
A developer can render the current collected trace in the terminal and include it in failed-test diagnostics without building a full CLI or TUI.
Terminal rendering is presentation-only: it does not mutate events, change Run outcomes, or introduce printing or a renderer dependency into the Agent Loop.
Phase 1 introduces no database, durable event files, network logging, or RPC/network event streaming; the collected history disappears when the process exits.

required_tests: Final answer without a tool call
Tool result is included in the following model input
Tool failure is represented and returned to the model
Provider timeout or failure is normalized
A retryable provider exception still fails after one attempt; a tool failure does not automatically repeat executor execution
Invalid model-generated tool call is rejected as a structured failure
Cancellation prevents another step from being scheduled
Events have stable Run IDs and increasing sequence numbers
Inspect the full in-memory event sequence directly for expected model/tool ordering and terminal outcome
Failure paths emit the expected failure events; recoverable tool failure does not require run_failed if the model can continue
Cancellation between steps emits run_cancel_requested and run_cancelled with no subsequent model or tool work
Convert and serialize every collected Event to JSON-compatible data in memory across success, failure, and cancellation paths
Render a collected trace for terminal or failed-test diagnostics without changing the event list, sequence, or Run outcome
Core tests import no provider, RPC, MCP, or database SDK
deferred_decisions: Exact numeric defaults for execution limits
Concrete MCP transport and approved tool set
Durable event storage, persistence schema, and restart recovery in Phase 3
Concrete RPC transport and sequence-based event polling or streaming in Phase 4
Cancellation of in-flight provider and MCP operations
Event types beyond the minimum execution and lifecycle set
exit_condition: The deterministic core loop is complete, bounded, and independent of concrete transports and external SDKs; its ordered in-memory events are directly testable, JSON-serializable, and readable through a separate optional terminal renderer without durable storage.
